learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge on fluids, fluid classification, and hydrostatics.
Acquire knowledge on the continuity equation and energy equation.
Gain experience in the use of relevant mathematical background.
Provide experience in applying fluid mechanics and related mathematical principles to solve chemical engineering problems.
Be informed about Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluid flow in pipes.

syllabus_topics: Derivation and Application of Fundamental Equations
Flow Classification; Incompressible and Compressible Flow
Basic Applications with Newtonian and Non-Newtonian Fluids and Related Equipment; Flow in Pipes
bibliography: C., Geankoplis,” Transport Processes and Unit Operation”, Prentice Hall Int, Inc. 1993.
Haluk Örs, Akışkanlar Mekaniği. İstanbul : Boğaziçi Üniversitesi, 1999.
R. E. Bird, W.E. Stewart, E.N. Lightfoot,”Transport Phenomena”John Wıley & Sons Inc. Second Edition,2002
J. O. Wilkes,” Fluid Mechanics for Chemical Engineers”, Prentice Hall,1999.
